findings.location: contract.shapes[2] ("The failure shape (proposed): a decision that arrives too late")
findings.finding: The worked failure example is self-contradictory and cites an unregistered problem type. Its own description says twice that the run ended with the platform's registered `deadline-exceeded` problem (504, retryable), but the JSON example's `type` member is a different, never-registered suffix, `human-ask-expired`, carrying status 409 and `retryable: false` -- three fields (type, status, retryable) that disagree with the very outcome the prose just described. cap-errors owns the closed problem registry (docs/decomposition.md section 2.1.6) and states plainly that an unregistered type is a conformance failure and that a missing row is fixed by 1-3-1, never by minting a suffix at the call site; `human-ask-expired` has no row there. core-graph, written in this same wave, hit the identical gap (no registry row for a rejected graph edge) and handled it correctly: it opened an explicit open_question, named the type `graph-assertion-invalid` as 'proposed and pending registration', and specified that until the row lands an implementation returns the existing `document-invalid` type instead of inventing one. cap-human-interaction-use does none of that -- no open_question, no pending-registration marker, no fallback to a registered type -- and presents `human-ask-expired` as the wire type a caller should branch on.
findings.evidence: cap-human-interaction-use/skill.json: description "The run already ended with deadline_exceeded, so there is nothing to resume; a new run is the remedy, not a retry." and detail "ask-deploy-0001 expired at 2026-09-03T18:00:00Z after 8h open; the run terminated with deadline_exceeded." against the same example's own "type": "urn:agentic:problem:human-ask-expired", "status": 409, "retryable": false. docs/decomposition.md line ~412: "| `deadline-exceeded` | 504 | yes | Wall clock ceiling reached |" -- no `human-ask-expired` row exists anywhere in the ten-row registry. cap-errors/skill.json instructions step 3: "When a failure mode has no row in that registry, apply 1-3-1 rather than minting a suffix at the call site: state the problem, list the three best registry changes, follow the recommendation, and record it as an open question with the row you would add." core-graph/skill.json open_questions[0].default: "`urn:agentic:problem:graph-assertion-invalid`, marked proposed and pending registration; until the row lands, an implementation returns `document-invalid` with the offending edge in `causes` rather than inventing a type."
findings.suggested_change: Either (a) reuse the registered `deadline-exceeded` type in the worked example (matching the prose, status 504, retryable true) and drop the invented suffix, or (b) follow core-graph's pattern: add an open_question naming `human-ask-expired` as proposed and pending registration in docs/decomposition.md section 2.1.6, and fall back to an existing registered type (`deadline-exceeded` is the closest fit) until that row lands. Either way, make the example's type, status and retryable fields agree with whichever choice is made and with the prose describing it.

findings.location: cap-capability-registry-use: contract.shapes[1] and definition_of_done; cap-mandate-broker-use: contract.shapes[1] and definition_of_done; cap-memory-use: contract.shapes[2]
findings.finding: Three more -use skills in this wave each mint a brand-new `urn:agentic:problem:` suffix in a worked example and/or a definition_of_done's expected_failure text, and present it as the actual wire type a caller reads -- but none of the three suffixes (`record-unsigned`, `credential-audience-mismatch`, `memory-scope-denied`) has a row in cap-errors' closed registry (docs/decomposition.md section 2.1.6: document-invalid, criterion-unresolvable, identity-untrusted, policy-denied, budget-exhausted, deadline-exceeded, cancel-timeout, isolation-unavailable, adapter-unavailable, idempotency-conflict), and none of the three skills raises an open_question about registering it, the way core-graph did for the same kind of gap in this same wave. `memory-scope-denied` (403, a deterministic pre-execution refusal on scope) is a close semantic match for the already-registered `policy-denied` (403, "A deterministic pre-execution refusal, carries rule_id"), which sharpens the case that this was a suffix invented at the call site rather than mapped to what already exists.
findings.evidence: cap-capability-registry-use/skill.json: "type": "urn:agentic:problem:record-unsigned" (contract.shapes[1]) and definition_of_done.expected_failure: "a problem details body whose type is `urn:agentic:problem:record-unsigned`". cap-mandate-broker-use/skill.json: "type": "urn:agentic:problem:credential-audience-mismatch" and definition_of_done.expected_failure: "a problem details body whose type is `urn:agentic:problem:credential-audience-mismatch`". cap-memory-use/skill.json: "type": "urn:agentic:problem:memory-scope-denied". None of `record-unsigned`, `credential-audience-mismatch`, `memory-scope-denied` appears in docs/decomposition.md's ten-row registry table (verified by grep over the section). None of the three skills' open_questions arrays mentions the registry, a pending type, or 1-3-1 (cap-capability-registry-use asks only about yanked versions; cap-mandate-broker-use only about parking work with no mandate; cap-memory-use only about scope widening). cap-errors/skill.json instructions step 3, same quote as C7-001: "apply 1-3-1 rather than minting a suffix at the call site ... and record it as an open question with the row you would add."
findings.suggested_change: For each of the three suffixes, either add an open_question following core-graph's exact pattern (name the type, mark it proposed and pending registration, and name the closest existing registered type to fall back on until the row lands), or, where an existing row already fits -- `policy-denied` for `memory-scope-denied` is the clear case, and `identity-untrusted` is a plausible fit for `credential-audience-mismatch` and `record-unsigned` -- reuse the registered type directly and drop the invented one.

brief_improvements: When a -use skill's worked failure example or definition_of_done needs a problem `type`, check it against docs/decomposition.md section 2.1.6's closed registry before writing it down, the same way core-graph checked before minting `graph-assertion-invalid`. If nothing fits, follow core-graph's pattern exactly: an open_question naming the type as proposed and pending registration, plus a stated fallback to an existing registered type until the row lands. Four of the five -use skills in this wave state a specific problem type at least once (cap-capability-registry-use, cap-human-interaction-use, cap-mandate-broker-use, cap-memory-use); core-graph, in the ideal facet of the same wave, is the one skill that got this right, so the discipline was available and simply wasn't carried into the -use facet's worked examples.
what_worked: All 430 rows across the 14 skills (238 origin=sourced, 134 origin=proposed, per the rows_of() counting tools/validate_skills.py itself uses) verified programmatically as true verbatim substrings of their cited kb records, including all 30 open_question rows and every contract.standards entry -- zero citation defects found, and python3 tools/validate_skills.py independently confirms this with 0 errors across the whole repository (73 skills, 92 warnings, all pre-existing and none touching this wave's 14 skills).

The wave-3c lesson landed exactly as the ceremony-06 improve record intended: core-graph, whose manifest note assigns it the -use skill's usability section since core has no separate -use facet, carries all three of TARGET T1's worked producer examples (human, event, agent) plus a worked rejection in references/graph-shapes.md, and tools/validate_skills.py's new per-piece check (added in ceremony 6 specifically for this class of skill) reports zero warnings against it.

composes_with for all 14 skills matches docs/skill-manifest.json exactly in both directions (builds_on and used_by), checked programmatically with no exceptions -- not even the usual root-skill asymmetry, since none of these 14 is agentic-stack itself.

Every one of the five spot-checked SKILL.md files (core-graph, cap-memory-use, cap-mandate-broker, cap-capability-registry-use, cap-human-interaction-implement) is byte-identical to a fresh render of its skill.json, confirmed by copying each skill directory to a scratch location and diffing tools/render_skill.py's output against the committed file.

Honest claimed/measured discipline held throughout: every definition_of_done across all 14 skills is labelled claimed, every one names the proposed tool that does not yet exist, and none upgrades a design claim to a measurement -- including the adapter pairs' 'today' rows, which describe something PASS.md records as actually running (the A2 approve unit, the A3 vsock broker) but are still labelled claimed because no conformance run has been executed against them in this tree.

The proposed-entity-id discipline for the three capabilities PASS.md has no B3 row for (cap-human-interaction, cap-mandate-broker, cap-memory) is applied consistently: their adapter and swap-candidate entities are correctly omitted from the top-level entities[] array (which validate_skills.py checks resolve to real kb ids) and instead carried as proposed ids inline in the adapters[] rows and an open_question, exactly matching cap-capability-registry's precedent for the one capability that does have real adapter entities to cite.
